- **Integrity**: employees may fall victim to targeted social engineering attacks
- **Availability**: increased spam volume can overwhelm email systems
checks.reason: Reference inventory retained; provider is outside the current four-provider runtime and no predicate is implemented

checks.title: Cloudflare Zone Firewall Rules Use Blocking Actions to Protect Against Threats
checks.rationale:
Firewall rules configured only for **logging** provide visibility but no protection.
- **Confidentiality**: malicious traffic can access and exfiltrate sensitive data
- **Integrity**: application exploits can modify data without being blocked
- **Availability**: credential stuffing and abuse attacks reach the origin unimpeded
checks.reason: Reference inventory retained; provider is outside the current four-provider runtime and no predicate is implemented

checks.title: Hotlink Protection is enabled
checks.rationale:
Without **Hotlink Protection**, external websites can embed your media directly.
- **Confidentiality**: content may be used without proper attribution or permission
- **Integrity**: unauthorized use of media may misrepresent your brand
- **Availability**: bandwidth theft increases costs and may degrade performance
checks.reason: Reference inventory retained; provider is outside the current four-provider runtime and no predicate is implemented

checks.title: HSTS is enabled with recommended max-age and includes subdomains
checks.rationale:
Without **HSTS**, browsers may initially connect over HTTP before redirecting to HTTPS.
- **Confidentiality**: creates a window for SSL stripping attacks where attackers downgrade connections to unencrypted HTTP
- **Integrity**: first request can be intercepted and modified before HTTPS redirect
- **Session hijacking**: cookies and credentials may be captured during initial HTTP request
checks.reason: Reference inventory retained; provider is outside the current four-provider runtime and no predicate is implemented

checks.title: Always Use HTTPS is enabled
checks.rationale:
Without **automatic HTTPS redirects**, users may access resources over unencrypted HTTP.
- **Confidentiality**: traffic can be intercepted and read by attackers on the network path
- **Integrity**: HTTP responses can be modified in transit (content injection, malware insertion)
- **Authentication**: session cookies and credentials may be transmitted in plaintext
checks.reason: Reference inventory retained; provider is outside the current four-provider runtime and no predicate is implemented

checks.title: IP Geolocation is enabled
checks.rationale:
Without **IP Geolocation**, geographic-based security controls cannot be implemented.

- **Integrity**: cannot enforce geographic data residency requirements

checks.title: Minimum TLS version is set to 1.2 or higher
checks.rationale:
Allowing **legacy TLS versions** (1.0, 1.1) exposes connections to known protocol vulnerabilities.
- **Confidentiality**: BEAST, POODLE, and weak cipher suites can be exploited for traffic decryption
- **Compliance**: TLS 1.0/1.1 are deprecated by PCI-DSS, NIST, and major browsers
- **Integrity**: downgrade attacks can force weaker encryption that is susceptible to tampering
checks.reason: Reference inventory retained; provider is outside the current four-provider runtime and no predicate is implemented

checks.title: Rate limiting is configured for the zone
checks.rationale:
Without **Rate Limiting**, applications are vulnerable to volumetric attacks.
- **Confidentiality**: credential brute forcing can compromise user accounts
- **Integrity**: API abuse can manipulate data through excessive requests
- **Availability**: volumetric attacks can exhaust resources causing service degradation
checks.reason: Reference inventory retained; provider is outside the current four-provider runtime and no predicate is implemented

checks.title: CAA record exists with issue or issuewild tag
checks.rationale: Without **CAA** records or `issue`/`issuewild` tags, any certificate authority can issue certificates for your domain. Unauthorized certificates enable **man-in-the-middle attacks** and domain impersonation. CAA records with only `iodef` tags do not restrict certificate issuance.

checks.title: DKIM record exists with valid public key
checks.rationale: Without **DKIM** or with a revoked/empty public key, recipients cannot verify messages were sent by authorized servers. Attackers can forge emails from your domain, and content integrity cannot be proven. DMARC policies relying on DKIM will fail, affecting deliverability. A DKIM record with empty `p=` indicates a revoked key.
checks.reason: Reference inventory retained; provider is outside the current four-provider runtime and no predicate is implemented

checks.title: DMARC record exists with enforcement policy (p=reject or p=quarantine)
checks.rationale: Without **DMARC** or with `p=none`, there is no active protection against email spoofing. Attackers can spoof emails for **phishing campaigns** to steal credentials. Domain reputation is damaged by spoofed emails. The `p=none` policy only generates reports but does not block or quarantine spoofed emails.
checks.reason: Reference inventory retained; provider is outside the current four-provider runtime and no predicate is implemented

checks.title: SPF record exists with strict policy (-all)
checks.rationale: Without **SPF** or with a permissive policy (`~all`, `?all`, `+all`), attackers can forge emails from your domain. Phishing attacks can harvest sensitive information from recipients who trust spoofed emails. checks.title: Under Attack Mode is disabled during normal operations

checks.title: SSL/TLS encryption mode is set to Full (Strict)

checks.title: TLS 1.3 is enabled

checks.title: Universal SSL is enabled

checks.title: WAF is enabled

checks.title: E2E Networks VPCs have attached nodes

checks.title: E2E Networks VPC peering does not use external peers

checks.title: E2E Networks nodes have compliance mode enabled

checks.rationale: Publicly invocable Cloud Functions expose **business logic** to the internet and let any caller trigger execution. This enables **unauthorized data access** when the function returns sensitive output, **code execution** in shared environments, and **denial-of-wallet** attacks driven by uncontrolled invocation costs.

This may violate ISMS-P 2.7.1 and regulatory requirements for sensitive or personal data.

- Confidentiality: secrets bound to TPM exposed
- Availability: malicious boot code can brick VMs

checks.title: Vercel production deployments originate from a stable branch
